findings.where: Article specimen: the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop-03, phone-02)
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in the logo blue. The tile's own palette gives that colour to links and the button. A whole blue sentence reads as a link but goes nowhere (parts.txt marks it static), and in an article it competes with the real blue link below it.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on an article page clicks the quote expecting a source or a related piece, and gets nothing. Angélique will reuse the pull-quote style in every post, so the link colour stops meaning 'link' across the whole blog.

findings.where: Hero subhead, 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience' (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The first screen ends its pitch with a size claim, a count of years, instead of a checkable fact. It also sits right beside the checkable fact that is stronger: former Lead Lawyer in the World Bank's PPP Group.
findings.who_objects: Procurement staff at a multilateral bank judge an advisor on named roles and bodies, not on years. The brief asks for 'one strong line, no boasts', and this sentence reads as the firm voice Mark wants to leave behind.

findings.where: First screen and motion sketch, as a whole (desktop-01, phone-01, desktop-03)
findings.fault: The tile never shows how 'calm first' is met. The headline, subhead and 'Get in touch' button are all there from the first frame. The only motion is the heading rising in 580 ms, so text is asking before any quiet picture or moment has come.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder: client value 2 says every tile answers 'one quiet moving picture or moment before any text asks for anything'. Without it, the layout and animation rounds get no guidance on where the calm moment sits in this direction.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the principle words 'precise, light, quick' (desktop-02, phone-02)
findings.fault: This is the largest heading in the motion block, but it is set in Source Sans 3 semibold. The tile's own type-pair note limits Source Sans to 'the nav, buttons, labels and dates only' and gives headings to Gelasio SemiBold. The tile breaks its own rule.
findings.who_objects: The designers of round 2 and round 9, who build from this tile, get two answers for what a heading is set in. Angélique, copying styles, gets the same mixed signal.

findings.where: Style-tile section labels: 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' have a hairline rule under them; 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' do not (desktop-02, phone-01, phone-02)
findings.fault: Labels of one kind get two treatments, so the tile's sections look unevenly finished and the rule looks accidental, not like a system.
findings.who_objects: A designer reading the tile as the source of truth for section headings can't tell which treatment is the house one.

findings.where: Header logo at phone width (phone-01) against desktop (desktop-01)
findings.fault: At 390 px the lockup drops 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services' and keeps only the mark and 'MMM INFRA'. That is a logo version the client has not supplied or approved, and the brand sheet describes the mark with the descriptor set to its right.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo is a fixed asset 'never redrawn'. A phone visitor coming from LinkedIn also loses the only place the header says what MMM Infra is.
